function.name: launch_or_open
function.description: Open a program or a website on this PC by name. Examples: steam, discord, notepad, spotify, epic games, youtube, github, google, wikipedia. You may name several (e.g. 'steam and youtube'). The tool decides whether each name is an app or a website.

name.description: Name of the program or website to open.

function.name: run_command
function.description: Run a shell command on this Windows PC and return its output. Use it to build, test, install, debug or check system info: python, pip, git, npm, node, dir, tasklist, systeminfo, ping, etc. Runs in the workspace folder by default. Max 45 seconds; output truncated to ~8 KB. Disabled in PLAN mode.

command.description: The command to run, e.g. 'python tools/screenshot.py'.

workdir.description: Optional folder to run in: absolute path or relative to the workspace.

function.name: run_code
function.description: Run a small snippet of Python or Node.js in a sandboxed environment and return its output. Use it to test functions, verify logic, parse data or prototype before touching real files. The sandbox has no network and a 30s timeout.

function.name: web_search
function.description: Search the internet when you need up-to-date information, facts, news, documentation or anything you are not sure about.

function.name: web_fetch
function.description: Fetch and read the full text of a webpage by URL (use after web_search).

function.name: list_dir
function.description: List files and folders inside the workspace folder (paths are relative to it).

path.description: Relative path inside the workspace, e.g. '' (root).

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file inside the workspace folder (relative path).

function.name: search_files
function.description: Regex search across files in the workspace folder; returns file + line matches.

path.description: Optional relative folder to search inside.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create or overwrite a text file inside the workspace folder (relative path). Use only when the user asks to write or create a file.

function.name: edit_file
function.description: Replace text inside an existing workspace file (replaces ALL occurrences of old_text with new_text).
